newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Two Australians dead at Israel games.
newsitem.headline: Two Australians dead at Israel games.

text.p: Two Australians died and scores were injured when a bridge collapsed at the opening of an international Jewish sporting event in Israel, officials said on Tuesday.

Competitors from the 370-member Australian team were standing on a temporary bridge over the Yarkon River on Monday ready to lead a march into the Ramat Gan Stadium near Tel Aviv for the 27-nation Maccabiah Games when the bridge collapsed.

"We were walking across. All of a sudden we heard a bang," Australia team manager Harry Purcell told reporters. "And then all of a sudden in slow motion it just collapsed in the middle and we started to slide."

Charles Kaplan, president of the New South Wales state Jewish sports organisation, named the two dead delegation members as ten-pin bowler Greg Small, 37, and 50-year-old Yetty Bennett, section manager of the men's bowling team. Both were from Sydney.
The games, nicknamed the "Jewish Olympics", were postponed for a day of mourning.
Hospital officials said on Tuesday 43 people injured in the collapse of the wooden bridge were still in hospital including seven who sustained severe wounds.
The bridge was built specially for the event and was checked by construction engineers before the ceremony began, officials said.
"The plan was apporved by a construction engineer. After the bridge was built we brought an engineer to check it and he gave his approval," said Yoram Eyal, head of the event's planning commmittee.
He denied receiving a police warning before the ceremony that the bridge was unsafe.
Police launched an investigation but said there was no suspicion of foul play.
"I assume during the investigation...we will have to also question the people who built it," said Tel Aviv district police chief Shlomo Aronishki.

Organisers cancelled the march of national teams but a public storm erupted among organisers and politicians over the decision to proceed with entertainment for the 50,000 spectators present for the start of the quadrennial games.
A wet, shoeless and shirtless Australian named Zorek, a 15-year-old tennis player, described what he said was the worst experience of his life.
"I was under the water. I thought I was going to die. My head was under the water. I couldn't breathe for a minute until I felt the ground."
A cluster of youngsters in muddied white sports uniforms stood amid the rubble of the bridge moments after it collapsed into the water.
Some 40 minutes later, while rescuers formed human chains and marched into the marshy waters, Israeli President Ezer Weizman declared the games open.
"I am sorry this is the way to open the Maccabiah which should be more joyous and I hope that in this Maccabiah that there will be accomplishments that will make all of us happy," he told the crowd.
